title.narrative: Sustainable and resilient livelihood basis of conflict affected vulnerable rural households in Irob District

description.narrative:
Before the war of 2020, drought-prone Eastern Tigray was already chronically food insecure with severely constrained livelihood options. Crop production covered only a quarter of poorer households' food needs, and cash income opportunities were few. The devastating violent conflict came on top of the extreme drought in 2019 and the locust invasion and Covid-19 restrictions in 2020. The WFP FEWS network has labeled the food situation in Tigray in February 2022 as ‘famine’ (phase 5).
This program, carried out in the immediate aftermath – or even in a latent context – of severe violence, aims to improve in a structural way the livelihood base of conflict-affected vulnerable households, mainly female headed and landless households.

By the end of the project period, conflict affected vulnerable rural households, especially landless and female headed households, in 4 tabias (Endalgeda, Weraetle, Daya Alitena, Arae) of Irob district have an improved sustainable livelihood basis that is more resilient to economic, climate, and humanitarian crises, and enables them to seize opportunities and realize aspirations.

Total of 1300 conflict affected vulnerable HH : a) 800 HH - Result 2: • Mainly landless or resourceless • At least 50% FHH (400 FHH) • MHH: landless but settled prioritized • 60% LHH (480 LHH - Landless Households)
b) 500 HH - Result 3: • HH w/ focus on farm resilience
- 10 schools - 16 solidarity and cohesion promoting dialogue groups - 16 resource governance committees - 40 SILC - Government services of 4 tabia

description.narrative: Result 1: By the end of 2026, the capacity of communities in the four targeted kebeles to prevent and manage resource-use related conflict in a (gender) equitable way is strengthened.

title.narrative: IOV T1.1: % of households that perceive improvements in their community's capacity to peacefully manage conflicts arising from use of community resources.

IOV T1.2: % of surveyed households reporting that the majority of community members and vulnerable groups in the kebele are ensured of access to community resources (closed areas, grazing lands, irrigation facilities, water points, ...).
IOV W1.1: % of households that perceive improvements in their community’s capacity to peacefully manage conflicts arising from use of community resources.

IOV W1.2: % of surveyed households reporting that the majority of community members and vulnerable groups in the kebele are ensured of access to community resources (closed areas, grazing lands, irrigation facilities, water points, …).

description.narrative: Result 2: By the end of 2026, 830 very poor households (430 in Tigray, 400 in Wolaita), especially landless and female-headed households, have improved access to and use of financial and technical capacity building services that enable them to strengthen their livelihood basis.

title.narrative: IOV T2.1: % of targeted households reporting that their productive assets base increased thanks to their participation in the program.
IOV T2.2: % of targeted households reporting that their participation in SILC groups positively contributed to their household asset building process.
IOV W2.1: % of targeted households reporting that their productive assets base increased thanks to their participation in the program.
IOV W2.2: % of targeted households reporting that their participation in SILC groups positively contributed to their household asset building process.

description.narrative: Result 3: By the end of 2026, 800 vulnerable smallholder farmers (200 in Tigray, 600 in Wolaita) have improved their capacity (knowledge and skills) to increase and/or sustain their farm production in the face of climate change induced shocks and stresses.

title.narrative: IOV T3.3: % of targeted smallholder farmers who perceive a positive change of their farm production thanks to implementing resilience design at their farm.
IOV W3.3: % of targeted smallholders who perceive a positive change of their farm production thanks to implementing resilience design at their farm.
IOV T3.2: % of targeted smallholder farmers scoring high on the soil health index thanks to implementing the resilience design approach.
IOV W3.2: % of targeted smallholders farms scoring high on the soil health index thanks to implementing the resilience design approach.

description.narrative: Result 4: By the end of 2026, the program's stakeholders mutually reinforced each other around converging themes, capitalising on good practices.
